What the honors mean

Indiana teams are ranked by district points. A team's total counts only its first two home district events plus the state championship, where points are multiplied by 3. Offseason events such as Monster Match are unofficial: they award no district points and don't affect advancement.

Playoffs

Event winner

The team's three-robot alliance won the event's playoffs. Winners earn a blue banner, the sport's version of a championship pennant.

After qualification matches, eight alliances of three teams play a double-elimination bracket. The finals are best two out of three. Winning the state championship also earns a FIRST Championship spot.

District points: 20 points for finishing first, plus 5 for each finals match the team played in and won (up to 10 more). Maximum 30.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501) at FIN District Lafayette Event, Mar 28, 2026.

Source: FIRST

Runner-up

The alliance reached the finals and lost. Same as finishing second in a bracket tournament.

Only two of the eight alliances reach the best-of-three finals. Reaching it means the alliance survived the double-elimination bracket from at least one side.

District points: 20 points.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501) at Monster Match, Oct 31, 2026. Offseason event: no district points.

Source: FIRST

3rd or 4th place

The alliance went deep in the bracket but was eliminated before the finals.

In the double-elimination bracket, the loser of match 13 places 3rd and the loser of match 12 places 4th. Alliances knocked out earlier don't earn playoff points.

District points: 13 points for 3rd place, 7 points for 4th place.

Most recent: The Gold Standard (9431), Olympus Robotics (4982), CyBears (10434), Knight Robotics (8103), Argyll Attack (8742) at Monster Match, Oct 31, 2026. Offseason event: no district points.

Source: FIRST

Alliance selection

Alliance captain

The team ranked high enough after qualification matches to lead its own playoff alliance and choose its partners.

The top eight teams in the qualification rankings become captains in rank order. Qualification rank comes from ranking points earned in matches with rotating partners. If a captain is picked by a higher captain, the next-ranked team moves up.

District points: 17 minus the alliance number: 16 for the #1 alliance captain, 9 for #8.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501), Olympus Robotics (4982), CyBears (10434), Cyber Knights (8432) at Monster Match, Oct 31, 2026. Offseason event: no district points.

Source: FIRST

Drafted

Another team chose this team as a playoff partner. Getting picked means other teams' scouts rated the robot highly.

Captains pick in a serpentine draft: round one goes from alliance 1 to 8, round two back from 8 to 1. Teams scout every match to decide who to pick.

District points: 17 minus the order the team accepted: for example, 12 points for the fifth team to accept.

Most recent: The Gold Standard (9431), Knight Robotics (8103), Carroll Charger Robotics (10332), Argyll Attack (8742), G-Code Generals (10411) at Monster Match, Oct 31, 2026. Offseason event: no district points.

Source: FIRST

Advancement

State qualifier

The team earned a spot at the FIRST Indiana State Championship, the top 38 or so teams in Indiana.

Spots go mostly by district points from the team's first two home district events. FIRST Impact Award winners also qualify. Engineering Inspiration and Rookie All-Star winners qualify to compete for those awards. Indiana's championship holds 38 teams in one division.

District points: Everything earned at the state championship counts triple.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501), Iron Legends (9119), The Gold Standard (9431), Olympus Robotics (4982), CyBears (10434) at FIRST Indiana State Championship, Apr 19, 2026.

Source: FIRST

World Championship

The team earned a trip to the FIRST Championship in Houston, the sport's world finals.

Indiana has 12 FIRST Championship spots. They go first to the state championship's Impact, Engineering Inspiration and Rookie All-Star winners and its winning alliance, then to the highest remaining teams in district points. At Houston, teams are split into divisions such as Archimedes.

District points: Not counted in district points; it's the end of the season.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501) at FIRST Championship · Archimedes Division, May 2, 2026.

Source: FIRST

Judged awards

Imagery Award

Recognizes a team whose robot and team appearance look great together.

FIRST: it “celebrates attractiveness in engineering and outstanding visual aesthetic integration of machine and team appearance.” Named in honor of Jack Kamen.

District points: 5 points.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501) at FIN District Mishawaka Event, Mar 8, 2026.

Source: FIRST

Innovation in Control Award

Recognizes clever engineering in how the robot is controlled: its wiring, mechanisms or code.

FIRST: it “celebrates an innovative control system or application of control components – electrical, mechanical or software – to provide unique machine functions.” Judges interview the team in the pits.

District points: 5 points.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501) at FIN District Lafayette Event, Mar 28, 2026.

Source: FIRST

Quality Award

Recognizes the best-built robot: sturdy, well designed and well made.

FIRST: it “celebrates machine robustness in concept and fabrication.”

District points: 5 points.

Most recent: Team THRUST (1501) at FIRST Indiana State Championship, Apr 19, 2026.

Source: FIRST

Judges’ Award

A judges’ choice award for something special about a team that other awards don't cover.

FIRST: “the judging panel may decide a team’s unique efforts, performance, or dynamics merit recognition.”

District points: 5 points.

Most recent: Carroll Charger Robotics (10332) at FIN District Lafayette Event, Mar 28, 2026.

Source: FIRST

Rising All-Star Award

Recognizes a young team that is succeeding despite being new or rebuilding.

FIRST: it “celebrates the team that has persisted through challenges, despite the difficulties of being young. This could be the result of being a new team, or a team with recent turnover in membership.” It replaced the Rookie Inspiration Award in 2025; teams don't have to be rookies.

District points: 5 points.

Most recent: Apex Archers (10172) at FIN District Lafayette Event, Mar 28, 2026.

Source: FIRST

Individual honors

FIRST Leadership Award semifinalist

An honor for one student, not the team. Teams nominate student leaders, and nominees are recognized as semifinalists at district events.

Formerly called Dean’s List. Indiana names two finalists who go on to the FIRST Championship. Because it's an individual award, it isn't in the team district-points table.

District points: No team district points.

Most recent: Robo-Knights (8431) at FIN District Columbus Event, Mar 22, 2026.

Source: FIRST

The 2026 game

How a match works

FIRST reveals a new game every January. In 2026 it was REBUILT: two of three robots score “fuel” into their hub, then climb the tower before time runs out.

  1. 0:00–0:20

    Autonomous

    Robots run on their own code, with no drivers. They score fuel into their alliance’s hub, and some climb the tower for extra points.

  2. 0:20–2:40

    Driver control

    Students take the controls for 2 minutes 20 seconds. Fuel comes from the human player, the depot, or the middle of the field.

  3. Shifts

    Hubs take turns

    Based on how autonomous went, the two hubs switch between active and inactive. While your hub is off, you collect fuel or play defense.

  4. Endgame

    Climb the tower

    As time runs out, both hubs open up and robots climb the tower for points and ranking bonuses. The alliance with the most points wins.

Game description from FIRST’s official REBUILT game overview. The 2027 game will be revealed on January 9, 2027.

New to robotics?

The sport in 60 seconds

What are FRC and FTC?

They’re two competition formats run by FIRST. FRC (FIRST Robotics Competition) is for grades 9–12 and uses industrial-size robots that can weigh more than 100 pounds. FTC (FIRST Tech Challenge) is for grades 7–12 with smaller robots. Each has its own game, season and championship. Schools choose a format; it isn’t assigned by enrollment like football classes.

How does a match work?

Two alliances, red and blue, of three FRC teams each. In 2026 a match lasted 2 minutes 40 seconds: 20 seconds of autonomous, when robots run on code alone, then 2 minutes 20 seconds with student drivers. Partners change every qualifying match; then the top teams pick partners for the playoffs. See how the 2026 game worked.

How does the season work?

A new game is revealed in January (FRC) or September (FTC). FRC teams build a robot in weeks, play district events in March and April, and the best advance to the Indiana State Championship and the FIRST Championship in Houston.

What’s EPA?

Expected Points Added, from Statbotics: the average points a robot is estimated to add to its alliance’s score. It’s a performance rating, like points per game, not a measure of everything a team does.

Is it only about the robot?

No. Awards like Impact, Engineering Inspiration, Judges’ and Rising All-Star recognize outreach, design, business plans and student leadership. Many students go on to engineering, software and manufacturing careers.

Fast facts

Northeast Indiana has 12 FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) teams for high-school students and 3 FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) teams to follow in The REFINERY's 12-county region. In 2026 they won 4 district event titles and 7 judged awards, and 1 teams reached the World Championship in Houston. Team THRUST (1501) of Huntington County 4-H Robotics led the region in official district points. Together the region's FRC teams have earned 21 blue banners. The 2027 FRC season starts with the game reveal on Jan. 9, 2027. Source: The Blue Alliance and FIRST Indiana; site by The REFINERY, a Fort Wayne nonprofit robotics makerspace.

Terms to know

FRC and FTC
FIRST Robotics Competition (high school, robots up to about 125 lb) and FIRST Tech Challenge (grades 7–12, smaller robots). Different games and different ratings.
Alliance
Teams play in alliances: three FRC teams (two in FTC) per side, red against blue. Partners change every qualifying match; top teams pick partners for the playoffs.
District points
The official FIRST Indiana standings. Teams earn points for qualifying wins, playoff runs and awards; points decide who goes to state and to Houston.
EPA
Expected Points Added, from Statbotics: an estimate of how many points a robot adds to its alliance’s score in an average match, like points per game. A model, so it can be off early in a season.
OPR
Offensive Power Rating, the FTC version of a per-match scoring estimate. Not comparable to FRC’s EPA.
Blue banner
What FIRST awards for an event win or a top team award. Teams hang them like championship banners in a gym.
Record (W-L-T)
Official match wins, losses and ties. Because partners change every match, a record reflects the team and its partners.
Rookie year
A team’s first FIRST season. Second-year teams are often called “sophomores”.
Where the numbers come from
Who runs this site

The REFINERY, a nonprofit robotics makerspace in Fort Wayne, built and maintains this page. The REFINERY and its affiliate BioNanomics are listed sponsors of FRC teams 4982 (Homestead), 8742 (Madison-Grant), 10172 (South Side), 10332 (Carroll) and 10434 (Northrop) and FTC team 22331 (Canterbury). Doug Horner of The REFINERY is a listed sponsor of 9431 (Snider), and FTC rookie team 36124 is based at The REFINERY. Sponsorships come from each team’s public listing on The Blue Alliance and FTCScout. Standings, records and ratings are taken as published by The Blue Alliance, Statbotics and FTCScout; no ranking is adjusted by hand.

Using names of students and coaches

Team pages list people only with the exact role and date found in a public source or confirmed by the team. Rosters change every season; confirm current captains and coaches with the team before publishing.
